extensionDescription: Filter GitHub pull request diffs with your own filters and see how much is left to review.
panelFilterEmpty: No files in this pull request match $1

panelNotLoaded.1: 1 file not loaded yet, so line counts are partial
panelNotLoaded.n: $1 files not loaded yet, so line counts are partial

panelAnnouncePartial.1: 1 of them hasn’t loaded yet, so line counts are partial.
panelAnnouncePartial.n: $1 of them haven’t loaded yet, so line counts are partial.

optionsTagline: Each filter becomes a button in the bar on a pull request’s changed files. Works on $1.
helpBody: Focus Diff shows a file when its path matches Include and doesn’t match Exclude. Both are JavaScript regular expressions (regex), tested against the full path, like src/components/Button.tsx, without regard to case. An empty Include matches every path.
helpTests: tests and stories, as an Exclude
helpAll: All is always available and shows every file.
globalHint: Each filter is a button in the bar, on every pull request.
reposHint: Extra filters that show up only on one repository, or on every repository of an owner.
tryHint: See which buttons would show a file, using what’s on this page, saved or not.
tryEmpty: Type a file path to check it.
tryOnlyAll: Only $1 shows this file. No filter matches it.
shareHint: Send your filters to a teammate, or bring in theirs.
copyHint: Copies every filter on this page, saved or not.
copyFallbackHint: Copying isn’t allowed here. Select the text and copy it yourself.
importHint: Paste what they copied. It replaces the filters on this page, and nothing changes until you save.
errorRepo: Use the repository’s path, like owner/name, or owner/* for every repository of an owner or group.
statusFixFilters: Some filters need fixing before you can save.
statusFixRepos: Check the repository names before saving.
statusSaved: Saved. Open pull requests update right away.
statusQuota: Your filters are over the 8 KB the browser syncs per item. Remove a few and try again.
importEmpty: That text has no filters in it. Ask your teammate to copy their filters again.
importInvalid: That text isn’t a copied set of filters. Paste exactly what $1 produced.
welcomeLead: Big pull requests mix the code you need to read with tests, generated files and things other people own. Focus Diff adds a bar to pull requests that shows only the files you pick, with the real count of what is left to review. It works on $1.
howStep1Body: Each filter you set up is a button in the bar on a pull request’s changed files. Only the files whose path it matches stay; pick another to add its files.
howStep2Body: The numbers are the files left to review, the lines they change and the time they take. Mark a file as viewed and they count down, until Done.
howStep3Body: The first button takes you to the next file left to review, then on to the next filter that has some. The conversations button steps through the review comments.
demoHint: Try it below: it’s the real bar, on a sample pull request.
recipesHint: Add the ones that fit how you review. They’re regular filters, so you can rename or tweak them later in settings.
recipeAddedNotice: Added $1. Open a pull request to try it.
recipeStackDescription: Review the UI and the API in separate passes, without tests and stories in the way.
recipeAreaTitle: Focus on one part of the codebase
recipeAreaDescription: Only the folder your team owns. Swap payments for your own path, and add it to a single repository if it only exists there.
recipeTestsTitle: Read the code before the tests
recipeTestsDescription: Two buttons: one hides tests, stories and mocks, the other shows only the tests.
recipeGeneratedDescription: Hide lockfiles, snapshots, minified files and build output that nobody reads line by line.
recipeInfraDescription: CI workflows, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes and YAML config, for the reviewer who owns the platform.
recipeDatabaseDescription: Migrations, SQL and schema files, which deserve a careful look before merging.
recipeDocsDescription: Markdown, text files and anything under docs/, for writers and product reviewers.
welcomeShortcuts: Without the mouse: $1 next filter, $2 previous, $3 all files, $4 next file to review.
optionsVersion: Focus Diff $1, open source under the MIT license
filtersEmptyWithExamples: No filters yet. Add one, or start from an example.
timeHint: Review time assumes about $1 changed lines an hour. Removed lines count a fifth, each file adds 15 seconds, and generated or lock files only add those 15 seconds.

imported.1: Imported 1 filter. Review it, then save.
imported.n: Imported $1 filters. Review them, then save.

statusChangedElsewhere: Filters changed in another window. Save to keep your edits, or reload to see the new filters.
panelNoComments: No conversations in these files yet
commandNextUnviewed: Go to the next file to review
panelTimeInfo: How the review time is worked out
lookHint: How the bar looks on pull requests. The preview changes as you edit; pull requests change once you save.
colorsHint: Pick a colour or type its hex code, like #bf3989. A colour left empty follows the provider’s theme, light or dark.
themeImportHint: Paste what they copied. It’s added to your themes, and nothing changes until you save.
themeImportInvalid: That text isn’t a copied theme. Paste exactly what $1 produced.

themesImported.1: Imported 1 theme. Review it, then save.
themesImported.n: Imported $1 themes. Review them, then save.

statusFixTheme: Check the theme’s name and colours before saving.
statusQuotaTheme: Your themes are over the 8 KB the browser syncs per item. Delete a few and try again.
reposEmpty: No repository has filters of its own yet.
popupReviewsEmpty: Nothing is waiting for your review.
popupMineEmpty: You have no open pull requests.
popupSignedOut: Sign in to GitHub in this browser to see your pull requests.
popupUnreadable: GitHub’s pages didn’t read as expected, so the lists may be out of date.
popupOffline: GitHub can’t be reached right now, so the lists may be out of date.
popupDoneHint: They come back on their own when something new happens.
notifyHint: Hear about your pull requests without keeping GitHub open.
notifyOnHint: Every $1 minutes, Focus Diff reads your GitHub notifications and pull request lists with the session you’re signed in with. Nothing goes anywhere but GitHub.
notifyBlocked: This browser hasn’t allowed Focus Diff’s notifications yet.
notifyDenied: The browser didn’t allow notifications, so they stay off.
notifyReposOnlyHint: Empty means every repository. owner/* takes all of an owner’s.
notifyEventReposHint: These take the place of the ones above for this event; empty goes back to them.
notifyQuietHint: The lists and the count keep updating; nothing pops up.
notifyGroupedOption: Sum several up in one notification
notifySticky: Keep on screen until I click
errorRepos: “$1” isn’t a repository path. Use owner/name, or owner/* for all of an owner’s.
eventReadyForReview: A draft becomes ready for review
eventCommentMineFull: Someone comments on my pull request
eventCommentReviewingFull: Someone comments on a pull request I review
statusFixNotify: Check the notification repositories before saving.
statusQuotaNotify: Your notification settings are over the 8 KB the browser syncs per item. List fewer repositories and try again.
notifyReviewRequestedTeam: $1 asked your team for a review
notifyReadyForReview: $1’s pull request is ready for your review
notifyCommentReviewing: $1 commented on a pull request you review
notifyChangesRequested: $1 requested changes on your pull request
reviewHint: Set aside time to review. When it comes, Focus Diff picks the pull requests that fit, by how long each one takes you.
reviewOn: Remind me when it’s review time
reviewOnHint: Pick when and for how long; you’re told what fits, and the time counts down on the toolbar icon.
reviewNoneNext: No review time is on. Turn one on, or give it a day and a time.
errorReviewSpan: The end comes before the start.
reviewOrderOldestHint: The oldest pull requests first, so nobody waits too long.
reviewOrderQuickestHint: As many as fit, the shortest first.
reviewOrderFillHint: The mix that uses the time best.
reviewFilesHint: Only these filters’ files count toward the time, and they’re on in the bar when you open one. A pull request with none of their files is left out; in a repository none of them are for, every file counts.
reviewNoFilters: With filters set up, a review time can count only their files, like only the backend.
reviewPaceHint: About $1 changed lines an hour, until your own pace is learned. The bar’s estimates use it too.
reviewLearn: Learn my pace from what I review
reviewLearnHint: On a pull request’s files, the time you’re active on each counts until you mark it viewed, per kind of file. A pause to think counts; past a minute and a half without moving, it stops. Kept on this device only.
reviewLearnedNothing: Nothing learned yet. Mark files as viewed as you review and the estimates follow you.
reviewUnviewed: Count only files I haven’t marked as viewed
reviewApplyFilters: Turn on the review time’s filters in the bar
reviewRemindEnd: Tell me when the time’s up
reviewSkipEmpty: Say nothing when there’s nothing to review
reviewHold: Hold every notification while I review
reviewHoldHint: They show once the time’s up.
reviewWhichWait: Pick which notifications always wait for review time
notifyWhenHint: You have review times: each event can show right away, or wait for your next review time, where it’s listed with what to review.
statusFixReview: Check the review times before saving.
statusQuotaReview: Your review times are over the 8 KB the browser syncs per item. Remove some and try again.

reviewTimeOffer.1: Review time: 1 pull request, about $2 min
reviewTimeOffer.n: Review time: $1 pull requests, about $2 min

reviewTimeNothing: Review time: nothing waiting for your review
reviewTimeOver: The one picked takes about $1 min, $2 min more than the $3 min set aside.

reviewTimeHeld.1: Also 1 update held for review time.
reviewTimeHeld.n: Also $1 updates held for review time.

reviewTimeAllDone: You went through all of them.
welcomeReviewHint: Pick one to start with. When it’s time, Focus Diff tells you which pull requests fit, by how long each takes you, and learns your pace as you go.
welcomeReviewCustomize: Make your own, or change these, in settings
welcomeReviewAdded: “$1” is set. Review requests now wait for it; change that in Notifications.
presetTwiceDescription: Half an hour mid-morning and mid-afternoon, so nobody waits more than half a day.
presetEveryDescription: Short passes through the working day that keep small pull requests moving.
presetEndDescription: One longer block to clear the queue before you log off.
reviewEstimatesHint: For review time, and for the time left in the bar on every pull request.
reviewTimeSignedOut: Review time: sign in to GitHub to see what’s waiting
reviewTimeUpUnknown: GitHub couldn’t be read to tell how far you got.
popupSkipping: Review times are skipped for now.

popupReviewNowHeld.1: Review now, 1 update kept for review time
popupReviewNowHeld.n: Review now, $1 updates kept for review time

reviewAgainFirstHint: When someone asks you to review a pull request again, it goes before the rest, if it fits.
reviewQueueEstimates: Show how long each pull request in the review queue takes
reviewQueueEstimatesHint: Focus Diff reads each pull request’s list of files from GitHub, once per push.
popupReposHint: Leave it empty to list every repository. owner/* covers all of an owner’s. With more than one repository listed, chips at the top narrow the list to one. The icon counts the same pull requests.
popupTeamsHint: Off, the queue lists only the pull requests you were asked to review by name. Notifications and review time follow the queue.
statusFixPopup: Check the review queue’s repositories before saving.
statusQuotaPopup: Your review queue settings are over the 8 KB the browser syncs per item. List fewer repositories and try again.
popupSettingsHint: Pick the repositories whose pull requests the toolbar button lists, in Review queue and in My PRs.
popupDraftsHint: These aren’t ready for review yet, so the counts leave them out.
